label_judgement_standard: actionable requires ALL THREE: (1) need category is explicit - naming the CATEGORY is enough, a specific product name is not required; (2) the current approach is unmet and the author is actively seeking a solution - complaining about it plus asking, or actively asking for recommendations / alternatives / how to choose; (3) it is the author's own decision - they hold or share the decision. Watching the market, researching for someone else, promoting their own product, or hunting for content ideas does NOT count. Missing any one of the three -> borderline; clearly unrelated -> not_actionable. Ground truth is PER-TESTSET: consistency constraints apply only within one testset, never across testsets, because each testset has a different buyer. Criterion (1) is judged by DEMAND DOMAIN, not by SKU: naming any purchasable or usable CATEGORY is enough - it does NOT have to match the product's own SKU exactly, but it MUST fall inside the demand domain the product can serve. IntentRadar demand domain = finding customers / customer acquisition / lead generation / getting users. IN domain: 'find customers', 'be found by customers', 'get users', lead gen, outreach that converts, monitoring communities for buying signals, cold-start acquisition. OUT of domain: landing pages, finding TikTok creators, fundraising intros, interview/residency trackers, generic 'growth' with no ask about reaching buyers. Criterion (1) can fail in two different ways and they map to different labels: (i) no category is named at all (the author only complains or asks 'what should I do') -> one criterion is missing -> borderline; (ii) a category IS named but it falls OUTSIDE the demand domain (a landing page when we sell monitoring, a fundraising intro, a speaking-practice method that explicitly excludes tools) -> the product cannot serve this person at all -> not_actionable. The test sentence: is there ANY way this product could serve this person? Yes -> borderline; No -> not_actionable. Two further rules: (a) If the author explicitly asks for something FREE (free sites, free tools, free resources), there is no current willingness to pay, so this is not purchase intent -> borderline. Do NOT lower it to not_actionable: the need is real and in domain and only the willingness to pay is missing, and willingness can change; only the disappearance of the need makes it not_actionable. (b) Asking others about their experience ('anyone have experiences with X', 'did you find it ...') is a research stage and does NOT satisfy criterion (3)'s own-or-shared purchase decision -> borderline. Do NOT lower it to not_actionable: research is often the step before a purchase. The test for criterion (3) is whether the author themselves is making the decision ('before we go further down this road' = yes; 'anyone have experiences' = no). (c) A first-person build-vs-buy question ('do you use a tool for it, or roll your own?', 'should I build this or buy it?', 'is there something off the shelf?') DOES satisfy criterion (2): the author is actively seeking a solution to their own unmet need, because they are explicitly weighing the purchase option. This differs from rule (b)'s research-stage pattern: asking whether an approach works at all ('anyone have experiences with X', 'did it work for you') evaluates the approach and does not yet seek a solution for the asker. The test is whether the ask explicitly puts BUYING on the table as one of the options the author is choosing between. Any exclusion reason must map back to one of the three criteria; a reason that is not in the standard is a private standard and is not allowed.
label_changelog: rev a: full-text re-review after a 650-char truncation during batch labeling hid intent statements in einprag; 1wqugoc not_actionable->borderline (full text ends 'how did you get your first few people to actually use it?'). rev b: 1wpda04 actionable->borderline on the grounds that no tool was named. rev c: 1wpda04 restored to actionable - rev b was a judgement error. The 'must name a product' test was wrong (the standard only requires naming the category), and it was applied by analogy to einprag posts 1wqss45/1woyfxm/1wqq2r3, which is invalid because ground truth is per-testset: those posts are not_actionable/borderline for a flashcard seller, but 'I need to find customers' is a core positive for a customer-acquisition tool. 1wplixs remains actionable (own unresolved buy-vs-build decision: 'Do you use a tool for it, or roll your own?' + 'before we go further down this road'). Labels: 2 actionable / 9 borderline / 126 not_actionable; 137 rows verified. rev d: NO label changes. Adds the DEMAND-DOMAIN definition of criterion (1) (demand domain, not SKU). Records a re-review of 1wplixs after judge v4.2.0 rejected it as 'market research for their platform, not a first-person purchase decision' - MAINTAINED as actionable: the author's product is a generic feed/web-event subscription service with no Reddit intent scoring, which is a different track and therefore not a competitor (competitor = someone selling the same kind of product, not anyone who also does scraping or subscriptions); and 'before we go further down this road' refers to building the scraping themselves, which makes this an unresolved buy-vs-build decision and a first-person purchase decision. Reviewed and maintained is a different state from never reviewed. Adds rule (c) (build-vs-buy questions satisfy criterion 2) at the engineer's request, to be mirrored into the judge prompt. HONESTY NOTE: a regex scan of all 348 posts in both testsets finds this build-vs-buy pattern in exactly ONE post (1wplixs). The rule is therefore a stated interpretation of the standard, not a generalisation validated on data, and the resulting change must not be reported as a measured model improvement - on a 2-positive testset it is not evidence of anything. Negative result worth recording: a buy-vs-build phrasing appears in 1 of 348 posts (0.3%) across both testsets, so this way of expressing intent is rare on Reddit and cannot be measured on a sample of this size. Naming convention: any change in judge numbers that is driven by this rule must be described as 'a change caused by a standard clarification', never as an improvement.
